content.comment_body: Hello, I recently purchased a new CD with [product_name] [version_no]. How can I display Czech characters? Thanks in advance for any guidance. [user_name]
Which operating system are you using? Is it Windows?
Please refer to this link for switching between languages using the language bar: [url]

Let me clarify: [product_name] [version_no] only offers ISO8859_1, ISO8859_5, ISO8859_9, or ISO8859_16 character sets. Not all Czech characters are available. Some letters like ý, á, í, é appear, but characters such as ě, š, č, ř, ž are not supported.

Here is my experience when selecting the Czech keyboard and GBK as the character set. If this doesn't resolve your issue, I'm unable to offer further assistance. You might need to submit a support request.

Many Czech special characters are included in ISO8859_2, but they are not shown on the [product_name] display. You can select these characters using the Czech keyboard layout and possibly view them on your PC during simulation, yet they won't appear correctly on the device display. Regards, [user_name]
Please see the attached file. This is a real example, not a simulation.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users find that [product_name] [version_no] and its display lack complete support for Czech character sets. While certain Czech characters can be entered and viewed in the software simulation, several key letters (such as ě, š, č, ř, ž) are missing on the device display, resulting in usability challenges for those working in Czech.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] and its display to offer full compatibility and correct rendering of all Czech language characters, both in simulation and on the actual hardware.
